headline: Asus ProArt 4K 160Hz display with built-in colorimeter
summary: The Asus ProArt PA27UCGE boasts a 27-inch 4K panel with a 160Hz refresh rate and 98% DCI-P3 coverage, aimed at creative professionals.
details: Asus has unveiled the ProArt PA27UCGE, a new 27-inch 4K display designed for creators. It features a high 160Hz refresh rate, which is uncommon for professional monitors, promising smoother visuals for editing and design work.

The display offers 98% DCI-P3 color gamut coverage, ensuring accurate and vibrant colors essential for video editing, photography, and graphic design. It also includes a built-in colorimeter for easy calibration.

An optional monitor hood is available to further enhance viewing accuracy by reducing glare and ambient light interference. This accessory is crucial for maintaining color consistency in various lighting conditions.

While specific pricing and availability details are yet to be fully announced, the ProArt series typically targets professionals willing to invest in high-quality display technology for their demanding workflows.

headline_marked: Major Labels Demand [[AI Slop Songs]] Be Banned From Global Charts
headline: Major Labels Demand AI Slop Songs Be Banned From Global Charts
summary: The music industry is pushing for new regulations to disqualify AI-generated tracks from chart rankings, citing concerns over authenticity and potential streaming fraud.
details: A coalition of major record labels, including Sony Music, Universal Music Group, and Warner Music Group, is urging chart companies worldwide to implement new rules. They argue that only songs primarily created by humans should be eligible for chart inclusion, and any AI involvement must be demonstrably lawful.

This move comes amid a surge of AI-generated songs flooding streaming platforms, with tens of thousands reportedly uploaded daily. Some of these synthetic tracks have already climbed to the top of prominent charts, sparking controversy and legal action.

Several major labels have filed lawsuits against AI music generators like Suno and Udio, accusing them of training their models on copyrighted music without proper authorization. The coalition emphasizes that music potentially involved in streaming fraud should not contaminate official rankings.

The pressure for AI transparency is mounting on streaming services. Industry bodies like the RIAA and IFPI have proposed a labeling system to identify AI-generated music, while companies like Apple are introducing AI 'Transparency Tags,' though their application is currently voluntary.

Meanwhile, AI music creation tools are becoming more accessible, enabling users to generate tracks from simple prompts. This rapid advancement poses significant challenges for copyright, artist compensation, and the integrity of music charts globally.
